title: Introduction Mans Purpose And The Declaration Of 2 Abysses

questions.question: What does the passage say is the main reason people are sent to this world?
questions.answer: To know their Creator, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What is described as the first and most basic duty of a human being?
questions.answer: Learning about Allah and having faith in Him and His oneness.

questions.question: How should a person accept Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: With submission and strong certainty.

questions.question: What two big hopes in human nature are mentioned?
questions.answer: Wanting life to last forever and having many endless hopes.

questions.question: What other side of human life is mentioned along with those hopes?
questions.answer: People also face many troubles and hardships.

questions.question: According to the passage, what things are the foundation and key of everlasting life?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowing Allah, and the ways that lead to that.

questions.question: How does the passage judge goals and achievements that are separate from faith and knowing Allah?
questions.answer: They are low in value, and sometimes not worth much at all.

questions.question: Why would worldly success alone not be enough for a human being, based on this passage?
questions.answer: Because people want lasting life, and only faith and knowing Allah truly lead to that.

questions.question: What can we infer about the value of worship from this passage?
questions.answer: Worship is one of the central reasons for human life, so it is very important.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: A person’s real purpose is faith, knowledge of Allah, and worship, not just worldly things.

questions.question: According to the passage, what gives human life its real purpose?
questions.answer: Recognizing Allah, believing in Him, and worshipping Him.

questions.question: Which is more important in the passage: collecting worldly things or growing in faith?
questions.answer: Growing in faith is more important.

questions.question: What does it mean that believing in Allah is an obligation on people?
questions.answer: It means it is a duty every person must carry.

questions.question: Besides belief, what kind of understanding is a person supposed to have about Allah?
questions.answer: A person should know Allah and accept that He is One.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human wishes and troubles?
questions.answer: Human wishes are very great, and their troubles are also very many.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect faith with eternal life?
questions.answer: Because faith and knowing Allah are presented as the way to gain everlasting life.

questions.question: If something does not help a person move toward Allah, how is it viewed here?
questions.answer: It is seen as small or even without real value.

questions.question: If a student used this passage to guide daily life, what should come first?
questions.answer: Faith, learning about Allah, and worshipping Him.

questions.question: What three connected parts of human purpose are named in the passage?
questions.answer: Knowing the Creator, believing in Him, and worshipping Him.

questions.question: Who is the Creator spoken about in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah, the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: What truth about Allah is especially named as part of human duty?
questions.answer: That He exists and that He is One.

questions.question: Is weak doubt enough for this duty, or is something stronger needed?
questions.answer: Something stronger is needed: sincere acceptance and firm certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say humans naturally long for?
questions.answer: Lasting life and never-ending existence.

questions.question: What does the passage show by mentioning both huge hopes and many hardships?
questions.answer: It shows that people need something greater than temporary worldly things.

questions.question: What is said to be the basis of eternal life?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and knowledge of Him.

questions.question: What else is included along with belief and knowledge as important for eternal life?
questions.answer: The means that help a person reach them.

questions.question: According to the passage, how should we view achievements that are cut off from faith?
questions.answer: We should see them as low and sometimes empty.

questions.question: What lesson does this passage teach about success?
questions.answer: Real success is not just gaining things in this world; it is reaching faith, knowing Allah, and worship.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about why human beings are in this world?
questions.answer: They are here to know Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What is the most important responsibility placed on human beings in the passage?
questions.answer: To know Allah and believe in His existence and oneness.

questions.question: How should this belief be held inside the heart?
questions.answer: With obedience and complete certainty.

questions.question: What kind of life do people naturally want, according to the passage?
questions.answer: A life that does not end.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the size of human hopes?
questions.answer: It says they are without limit.

questions.question: What does it say about human pains and problems?
questions.answer: They are also very great and wide-reaching.

questions.question: What are called the key to eternal life?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowledge of Allah, and the ways of reaching them.

questions.question: How are other goals measured when compared with these truths?
questions.answer: They are seen as lesser, and sometimes not truly valuable.

questions.question: What is one good summary sentence for this passage?
questions.answer: Human life finds its true meaning only through faith, knowing Allah, and worship.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the wisdom behind human life in this world?
questions.answer: Its wisdom is that people should recognize Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say comes before all other human duties?
questions.answer: Knowing Allah and believing in Him.

questions.question: What part of belief is mentioned besides believing that Allah exists?
questions.answer: Believing that Allah is One.

questions.question: What kind of inner state should go with this belief?
questions.answer: Submission and sure conviction.

questions.question: What deep desire in people shows that short worldly life cannot satisfy them?
questions.answer: Their desire for life that continues forever.

questions.question: What other part of human experience makes people need something greater than worldly success?
questions.answer: They go through many painful difficulties.

questions.question: In this passage, what makes eternal life possible?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah, knowing Him, and following the path to those things.

questions.question: If a person gains many things but has no faith, how does the passage rate those gains?
questions.answer: It rates them as low, and sometimes as having little real worth.

questions.question: What is the central teaching students should remember from this passage?
questions.answer: The greatest goal in life is to know Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What overall purpose of human life is given in the passage?
questions.answer: The purpose is to know the Creator, have faith in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the human duty toward Allah?
questions.answer: It describes it as the first and necessary duty.

questions.question: What must a person believe about Allah according to the passage?
questions.answer: That Allah truly is, and that He has no partner and is One.

questions.question: What quality should a believer have instead of shaky belief?
questions.answer: Strong certainty.

questions.question: What two parts of human nature are placed side by side in the passage?
questions.answer: Great hopes and many hardships.

questions.question: Which things are presented as the strong base for eternal life?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowledge of Allah, and the means to reach them.

questions.question: What happens to other achievements when they are compared with these eternal matters?
questions.answer: They become small in value, and sometimes almost worthless.

questions.question: What main message does this passage give to a Muslim student?
questions.answer: Your life’s highest goal should be faith in Allah, knowing Him, and worshipping Him sincerely.
